subject: general
question: Which of the following will show diffusion fastest?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gas in gas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Diffusion** refers to the process where particles move from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration until equilibrium is reached.
 
• In the case of gases, the particles are widely spaced, have high kinetic energy, and move at high speeds. This enables them to diffuse faster compared to solids or liquids.
 
• Among the given options, diffusion of **gas in gas** occurs the fastest because gases have negligible intermolecular forces and maximum freedom of movement.
 
• Comparatively, solids have tightly packed particles with strong intermolecular forces, making diffusion extremely slow. Liquids are denser than gases, so diffusion in liquids is slower than in gases but faster than in solids.
 
• The molecular velocity of gases is governed by the **Kinetic Molecular Theory**, which states that lighter gas molecules (low molecular weight) diffuse more rapidly than heavier ones. For example, hydrogen diffuses faster than oxygen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Diffusion in Solids:**

 
 
• Diffusion in solids is extremely slow because particles are closely packed and vibrate in fixed positions.
 
• This type of diffusion is usually observed in processes like alloy formation or interstitial diffusion in metals.
 
• Example: Diffusion of carbon atoms in iron to form steel.
 
 
 
• **Diffusion in Liquids:**
 
 
• Particles in liquids have more freedom of movement compared to solids but less than gases.
 
• Diffusion in liquids is slower than in gases due to higher density and intermolecular forces.
 
• Example: Diffusion of sugar in water.
 
 
 
• **Diffusion in Gases:**
 
 
• Gases exhibit the fastest diffusion due to high kinetic energy and negligible intermolecular forces.
 
• Example: The spread of perfume in a room.
 
• The rate of diffusion in gases can be mathematically represented by **Graham’s Law of Diffusion**, which states that the rate of diffusion is inversely proportional to the square root of the molar mass of the gas.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Diffusion Rate:**
 
 
• Temperature: Higher temperatures increase the kinetic energy of particles, accelerating diffusion.
 
• Medium: Diffusion is faster in less dense mediums (e.g., gases) and slower in denser mediums (e.g., solids).
 
• Particle Size: Smaller particles diffuse faster due to lower mass.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Real-life Applications of Diffusion:**

 
 
• Respiration: Oxygen diffuses into the blood from the alveoli in the lungs, while carbon dioxide diffuses out.
 
• Cooking: Aroma diffusion from spices or foods during cooking is an example of diffusion of gas in gas.
 
• Industrial Processes: Diffusion is crucial in processes like gas purification and separation techniques.
 
 
 
• **Graham’s Law of Diffusion:**
 
 
• This law states that the rate of diffusion of a gas is inversely proportional to the square root of its molar mass.
 
• Mathematically, Rate₁/Rate₂ = √(M₂/M₁), where M₁ and M₂ are the molar masses of gases.
 
• Example: Hydrogen diffuses approximately 4 times faster than oxygen due to its lower molar mass.
